target.title: fix(gateway): drain root work continuations before stop process exit
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105697

When a gateway process receives a direct stop signal (SIGTERM/SIGINT without a restart intent), any `session_end` plugin hooks that were already started by session reset/delete/compaction may be truncated before they complete. This happens because the session is removed from the shutdown tracker synchronously before the hook fires asynchronously via `runWithGatewayIndependentRootWorkContinuation`, and the direct-stop path (`handleStopAfterServerClose`) exits the process without waiting for these continuations to settle. Affected plugins may lose database writes, memory summaries, or external resource cleanups.

#### Why This Change Was Made

The existing shutdown drain (`drainActiveSessionsForShutdown`) only covers sessions still in the active-session tracker when shutdown begins. Sessions already finalized by reset/delete/compaction are deliberately excluded to avoid double-firing. Their `session_end` hooks already run as tracked gateway root work continuations — the only gap is that the direct-stop path never waits for the root work set to drain before exiting.

Instead of changing the `emitGatewaySessionEndPluginHook` signature (which would alter latency on every normal finalization path), this fix adds a bounded drain of the existing gateway root work set to the direct-stop path, matching the approach recommended by ClawSweeper in the issue review.

The drain uses a referenced `setTimeout` poll loop (not `.unref()`) so that the polling timer keeps the Node.js event loop alive during the wait. The wait is bounded at 2 seconds, and the caller always invokes `exitProcess(0)` after the drain returns. Per review clarification: the force-exit watchdog is cleared at line 705 of `run-loop.ts` before `handleStopAfterServerClose` is entered at line 710, so the drain does not depend on the watchdog — it is self-bounded by its own referenced timer and the unconditional `exitProcess(0)` that follows.

#### User Impact

No visible impact under normal operation. On graceful gateway stop, pending `session_end` hooks now have up to 2 seconds to complete before the process exits. The wait is bounded to 2 seconds with a referenced timer, and the caller unconditionally calls `exitProcess(0)` after the drain returns (even on timeout), so a stuck hook cannot block shutdown.

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes with no errors on changed files
- **Unit tests:**
  ```
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts

  ✓ |unit| src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts (17 tests)
  ✓ |cli|  src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts (45 tests)

  Test Files  2 passed (2) | Tests  62 passed (62)
  ```
- **Change scope:** 4 files, +116 lines
  - `src/process/gateway-work-admission.ts` — new `waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain` helper
  - `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.ts` — drain call in `handleStopAfterServerClose`
  - `src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts` — 4 new tests
  - `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts` — 2 new tests + mock fix
  - No config, CLI, SDK, docs, or changelog surface affected
- **No new dependencies**
- **Real gateway startup + shutdown log** (Node v22.23.1, 11 production plugins loaded):

```
[gateway] loading configuration…
[gateway] resolving authentication…
[gateway] starting...
[gateway] starting HTTP server...
[health-monitor] started (interval: 300s, startup-grace: 60s, channel-connect-grace: 120s)
[gateway] agent model: vendor/model-name (thinking=off, fast=off)
[gateway] http server listening (11 plugins: acpx, browser, canvas, device-pair, file-transfer,
           matrix, memory-core, ollama, phone-control, talk-voice, workboard; 4.1s)
[gateway] log file: /tmp/openclaw/openclaw-YYYY-MM-DD.log
[hooks] loaded 4 internal hook handlers
[matrix] [default] starting provider (http://10.x.x.x:xxxxx)
[plugins] embedded acpx runtime backend registered lazily
[gateway] ready
[heartbeat] started

--- SIGTERM received ---
[gateway] signal SIGTERM received
[gateway] received SIGTERM; shutting down
[shutdown] started: gateway stopping
[shutdown] completed cleanly in 852ms
```

- **Shutdown timeline:** SIGTERM → shutdown started (170ms) → server close + drain + cleanup → completed cleanly (852ms total). No hang, no crash, bounded exit.
- **Process-level proof** (real child processes, real SIGTERM, real production modules):
  ```
  $ node --import tsx _proof-gateway-drain.ts

  === Gateway Drain — Real Process Proof ===

  [Case 1] No pending hooks — drain returns immediately, exit 0
    exit=0, 17ms

  [Case 2] 350ms hook, SIGTERM mid-flight → drain waits, file persisted
    exit=0, 314ms, sentinel: done at 1783932907158

  [Case 3] Stuck hook (never releases) → timeout 1000ms, exit 0
    exit=0, 1023ms

  [Case 4] 2 concurrent hooks (150ms + 350ms) → drain waits for slowest
    exit=0, 318ms
    fast: done at 1783932909249
    slow: done at 1783932909450

  === Results: 12 passed / 0 failed ===
  ```

  - Case 1: empty queue → drain returns true immediately
  - Case 2: mid-flight hook → drain blocks until hook writes sentinel file
  - Case 3: stuck hook → drain returns false after 1s timeout, exits cleanly
  - Case 4: two concurrent hooks → drain waits for slowest, both files confirmed
